ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It features a dark brown to black body with distinct, narrow white or yellowish crossbands and a white, unpatterned belly. Key features include a flattened head.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Lycodon fasciatus* is the presence of distinct, complete white or yellowish rings that encircle the body, contrasting with its dark brown to black ground color.
ai.habitat: *Lycodon fasciatus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Himalayan foothills and Northeast India, typically ranging from 300 to 2,000 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Banded Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively prowling at night to hunt for small lizards and frogs among leaf litter and low vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon fasciatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–10 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon fasciatus* is found in Northeast India and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting forested regions at elevations ranging from 300 to 2,000 meters.
